title: Quiet Lights
statement: A row of `n` decorative lights can each be on or off, but two lights that are on may never stand next to each other (they would be too bright). Return how many on/off patterns of the row are allowed.
constraints: The answer fits in a 32-bit integer

answerKey.pattern: Recursion on the last light, with remembered results
keyPoints: If the last light is off, the rest is any allowed row of n - 1
If the last light is on, the one before must be off, so the rest is any allowed row of n - 2
patterns(n) = patterns(n - 1) + patterns(n - 2), with patterns(1) = 2 and patterns(2) = 3
Remember results so each n is computed once
edgeCases: n = 44 (plain recursion is far too slow)
acceptableSlowerApproaches: Try all 2^n rows and check each: far too slow
A loop keeping the last two counts: O(1) space

hints: Look at the last light. What are its two choices, and what does each mean for the light before it?
Off at the end leaves a row of n - 1; on at the end forces off before it and leaves a row of n - 2.
Add the two counts and store each result so it is not computed again.
